title: Limits
prerequisites: Ability to substitute a value into an algebraic expression.
Familiarity with the idea of a function.

topics.title: Concept of a Limit and Its Evaluation
topics.quick_summary: The limit of a function as x approaches a value is the value the function gets arbitrarily close to, which need not equal the function's value at that point.
topics.real_life: A car's speedometer reads instantaneous speed — the limit of average speed as the time interval shrinks towards zero.

detailed.definition: lim(x→a) f(x) = L means that f(x) can be made as close to L as desired by taking x sufficiently close to a, but not equal to a.
detailed.key_idea: A limit describes the approach, not the arrival. The function need not even be defined at x = a for the limit there to exist — which is exactly why limits are more powerful than substitution.
detailed.working_principle: If direct substitution gives 0/0, the expression is indeterminate and must be simplified by factorising, rationalising or using a standard limit before substituting again.
applications: The derivative is defined as a limit of a difference quotient.
Left-hand and right-hand limits must be equal for the limit to exist.

points: The limit exists only if the left-hand and right-hand limits are equal.
The limit at a point does not depend on the function's value at that point.
0/0 is an indeterminate form and needs algebraic simplification.
lim(x→a) [f(x) ± g(x)] = lim f(x) ± lim g(x), and similarly for products and quotients.
Standard limit: lim(x→a) (xⁿ − aⁿ)/(x − a) = n·aⁿ⁻¹.
mistakes: Writing 0/0 = 1 or 0/0 = 0; it is indeterminate, not a number.
Assuming the limit always equals the function's value at that point.
Applying the quotient rule for limits when the denominator's limit is zero.
topics.memory_hook: 'A limit is about the journey, not the destination' — where the function is heading, not where it lands.
topics.advanced: The formal ε–δ definition makes 'arbitrarily close' precise and is what put calculus on a rigorous footing in the nineteenth century. Every theorem of calculus ultimately rests on it.

formulas.name: Standard Algebraic Limit
formulas.variables: n = any rational number, a = the point of approach.
formulas.when_to_use: Whenever a limit produces the indeterminate form 0/0 with a difference of powers.
formulas.common_mistakes: Applying it when the denominator is not exactly (x − a).
formulas.shortcut: It is the derivative of xⁿ at x = a, written as a limit.
